request_outcomes.question: Does Medicare cover my dental appointment?
request_outcomes.answer: Medicare does not cover routine dental care, so dental appointments are self-pay for Medicare patients unless you also hold one of the accepted dental plans: Delta Dental PPO, MetLife PDP Plus or Guardian DentalGuard Preferred.

citations.chunk_text:
# Insurance plan guide
## Medicare and Medicaid

We accept Original Medicare (Part B) for medical visits. Medicare does not cover routine dental care, so dental appointments are self-pay for Medicare patients unless they also hold one of the dental plans listed in our dental care guide. We do not currently accept Medicaid or Medicaid managed care plans.

# Dental care guide
## Dental insurance

Medical insurance plans do not cover dental care. For dental appointments we accept these dental plans: Delta Dental PPO, MetLife PDP Plus and Guardian DentalGuard Preferred. We do not accept dental HMO (DHMO) plans, including Cigna Dental Care DHMO. If you do not hold one of the accepted dental plans, dental appointments are self-pay.

# Dental care guide
## What a dental appointment covers

A routine dental appointment includes an examination of your teeth and gums and a professional cleaning. Fillings and extractions are usually done at a separate appointment, once the dentist has examined you and explained the treatment.

# Dental care guide
## Services we do not offer

We do not offer teeth whitening, orthodontic treatment such as braces or clear aligners, or dental implants.

# Procedure codes and self-pay prices

Your itemized receipt lists each procedure done at your visit by its billing code. Medical procedures use five-digit CPT codes, and dental procedures use CDT codes that start with the letter D. If you pay out of pocket, each procedure below is charged at the price shown, in addition to the rate for the visit at which it is done.
